summary: Documents IANA assignments for CR-LDP extensions related to Automatic Switched Optical Network, an ITU-T architecture that adds a control plane to optical networks. It records the signaling extensions that the IETF's GMPLS work provides for ASON reference points.

plainLanguage.summary: This note is a record of the number codes used when optical network control messages use the CR-LDP signaling system.

subtitle: Code point assignments for optical network control protocols.

tldr.problem: Automatic Switched Optical Network (ASON) is an ITU-T architecture that adds a control plane to optical networks, but the IETF's GMPLS implementation (CR-LDP) needed IANA code point assignments for the protocol extensions.
tldr.mechanism: This document requests and specifies code points for CR-LDP extensions: two new messages (Call Setup and Call Release), four new TLVs (Call ID, Call Capability, Crankback, and others), and additional error codes for ASON-specific signaling.
tldr.outcome: The document allocates the necessary code points so that ASON control plane implementations can use CR-LDP for call and connection management over optical network reference points. It was updated by RFC 3468.

today: RFC 3475 is an Informational document published in March 2003. It was updated by RFC 3468, which consolidates and refines IANA assignments for multiple GMPLS protocols including this one.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.content:
Automatic Switched Optical Network (ASON) is an architecture specified by ITU-T Study Group 15 that adds a control plane to optical networks. The control plane uses signaling protocols to dynamically establish and manage optical connections.

The IETF selected Constraint-Based LSP Setup using LDP (CR-LDP) as one of the protocols for realizing ASON signaling. However, ASON requirements differ from the base CR-LDP specification, requiring new protocol messages and information structures. This document allocates the IANA code points required for these ASON-specific CR-LDP extensions, enabling interoperable implementations.
sections.plainLanguage: Optical networks need to automatically connect paths of light through the system. This document assigns ID numbers for the control messages that make this happen.

sections.title: Overview of CR-LDP Extensions
sections.content:
The ASON architecture requires several capabilities that the base CR-LDP protocol does not provide. The extensions cover:

Call and connection control separation: ASON distinguishes between calls (end-to-end service requests) and connections (individual network paths). CR-LDP is extended to support both logical separation (where call setup is accompanied by connection setup) and complete separation (where they occur independently).

Soft Permanent Connections (SPC): User-to-network segments are provisioned while the network segment is set up dynamically via the control plane, requiring support for the Egress Label TLV.

Crankback: When a connection request is blocked due to insufficient resources, the blocking node informs the requester of the location of the blockage, allowing rerouting attempts to avoid congested areas.

Additional error codes: ASON signaling requires error conditions not defined in base CR-LDP, such as invalid SNP IDs, unavailable resources, and security failures.
sections.plainLanguage: ASON needs more detailed ways to request and manage optical connections than the basic CR-LDP protocol provides. These extensions add the ability to split call setup from connection setup, handle blocked paths, and report specific errors.

sections.title: Call Setup and Release Messages
sections.content:
Two new messages are introduced for call operations:

Call Setup message (code 0x0500): Used when complete separation between call and connection control is required. It carries source and destination identifiers, a Call ID TLV, and a Call Capability TLV. The calling party sends this to initiate a call with no connection associated. The called party may accept or reject using an LDP Notification message.

Call Release message (code 0x0501): Sent by any network entity to terminate an established call. It must include the Call ID TLV identifying the call to be terminated. Reception of this message triggers release of all connections associated with that call, which then follow the normal CR-LDP Label Release and Label Withdraw procedures.
sections.plainLanguage: These two messages let you ask for a call to be set up (request a path through the network) and then tear it down when you are done. Each message carries the ID of the call so the network knows which one you are talking about.

sections.title: Protocol Data Structures (TLVs)
sections.content:
Four new Type-Length-Value (TLV) structures extend CR-LDP:

Call ID TLV (codes 0x0831 for operator-specific, 0x0832 for globally unique): Identifies a call globally or within an operator domain. The globally unique variant concatenates a global identifier (country code, carrier code, access point code) with an operator-specific identifier (network element address and local identifier). The operator-specific variant uses only the operator-specific portion. Call IDs remain constant for the lifetime of the call, and intermediate nodes must not alter them.

Call Capability TLV (code 0x0833): A 4-byte field that explicitly indicates the configuration capability of the requested call. The example given is 0x0000 for point-to-point calls.

Crankback TLV (code 0x0834): Used in LDP Notification messages to inform the requester that a Label Request was blocked. It contains an ER-HOP TLV indicating the location (an IPv4 or IPv6 address) where the resource shortage was detected, allowing the requester to compute a new route that avoids the congested area.
sections.plainLanguage: These structures carry information in each message. The Call ID says which call this is, Call Capability says what kind of service is being requested, and Crankback tells the sender where the network is too busy so it can try a different path.

sections.title: Error Codes and IANA Assignments
sections.content:
Seventeen new error codes are defined for ASON-specific conditions not covered by base CR-LDP. These include:

Invalid or unavailable Sub-network Point (SNP) IDs; Calling party busy; Invalid or unavailable Sub-network Point Pool (SNPP) IDs; Failures in creating Sub-network Connections (SNC) or Link Connections (LC); Invalid end-user names or Class/Grade of Service mismatches; Security check failures; Timeouts; and SNC/LC release failures.

The document also requests IANA allocation of the message codes (Call Setup 0x0500, Call Release 0x0501) and the four TLV codes listed in the previous section, ensuring that globally unique code points are registered in the LDP name space.
sections.plainLanguage: Optical networks encounter specific problems (like 'the destination is busy' or 'this security check failed'). The document defines error codes for these situations and reserves the numbering space so no two implementations accidentally use the same code for different things.
